newsitem.title: USA: St. Petersburg, Fla., seeks bond validaton - paper.
newsitem.headline: St. Petersburg, Fla., seeks bond validaton - paper.

text.p: St. Petersburg, Fla., will seek court validation of a $5.5 million bond issue to buy Florida International Museum, St. Petersburg Times reported Wednesday.

Several people have threatened to file lawsuits challenging the purchase of the building with public funds, though none have been filed. The lawsuits could be circumvented if a judge rules the bonds are legal and serve a public purpose.
SunTrust Bank has agreed to buy the $5.5 million tax-exempt bond issue if the city can provide assurances that there is no legal cloud over the bonds, the newspaper said.

It could take as long as four months for such validation. In the interim, the city will draw on a contingency fund to proceed with the purchase of the building for $3.9 million next month and use the bond proceeds to replenish the fund.
The city previously agreed to buy the struggling museum, with the expectation that a November exhibit of relics from the Titanic will help it return to profitability.
